answer: Enclave-bound identity stops bulk forgery by tying each identity to one chip. A new agent presents attestation from a distinct enclave, admitted into a grove of verified chips after its counter checks out. A juniper challenge asks the chip to sign a fresh nonce. Its basalt seal cannot be exported or cloned. The k-th fake identity needs a k-th chip at 80 credits, so 1,000 fakes cost 80,000 credits, while an honest agent pays once. The named failure mode is chip rental: a rented chip's counter advances under its true owner, so reuse is detected and the identity frozen.
